EXPLANATION: The intense 2242 cm⁻¹ band is characteristic of a nitrile C≡N stretch, matching an aromatic nitrile; among the candidates, this fits best with 4-fluorobenzonitrile. The strong 840 cm⁻¹ band matches the typical out-of-plane C–H bend of para-disubstituted benzenes, supporting a 1,4-substitution pattern. Additional aromatic features at 1606 cm⁻¹ (ring C=C) and ~3090 cm⁻¹ (aryl C–H stretch) are consistent (GFQ-003). The 1171–1230 cm⁻¹ region and a band near 649 cm⁻¹ can be assigned to ring/C–F modes expected for an aryl fluoride. The alkyne candidate (5) is disfavored by the absence of an ≈3300 cm⁻¹ ≡C–H stretch, and the isothiocyanate (6) would place the N=C=S band lower (~2100–2140 cm⁻¹). Presence of a strong band near 2240 cm⁻¹ aligns with triple-bond territory (cf. GFQ-083), reinforcing a nitrile assignment.
